@graph.definition: The value of the "sample standard deviation" of a set of measurements used to derive a mean value. Used to illustrate the extent of "dispersion" of the measurements from the mean. For data conforming to a normal distribution, 1 sigma encompasses about 68% of the expected values.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: An estimate of 1 standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean, derived from a particular sample of analysed data.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: The value corresponding to double the "sample standard deviation" of a set of measurements used to derive a mean value. Used to illustrate the extent of "dispersion" of the measurements from the mean. For data conforming to a normal distribution, 2 sigma encompasses about 95% of the expected values.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: An estimate of 2 standard deviations of the sampling distribution of the mean, derived from a particular sample of analysed data.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: The value corresponding to three times the "sample standard deviation" of a set of measurements used to derive a mean value. Used to illustrate the extent of "dispersion" of the measurements from the mean. For data conforming to a normal distribution, 3 sigma encompasses about 99.7% of the expected values.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: The interval, expressed as a deviation centered on the mean value (and calculated directly from the population observations), which will encompass the true value of the measured parameter 95% of the time, if the underlying statistical model is correct.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: The interval, expressed as a deviation centered on the mean value (and calculated directly from the population observations), which will encompass the true value of the measured parameter 99% of the time, if the underlying statistical model is correct.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: A circular 95 % confidence estimate for directional data. An angular estimate of the circle of 95% confidence (p = 0.05) about the mean direction.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: A dispersion parameter for directional data. "Delta" decreases as the directions become less dispersed. In practice, when the number of samples is greater than 10 - 20, delta is approximately equal to the circular (or angular) standard deviation.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: A precision parameter for directional data, measuring the concentration of the distribution about the true mean direction. The larger the value of Kappa, the more concentrated the direction; Kappa is 0 for a distribution of directions that is uniform over the sphere and approaches infinite for directions concentrated at a point.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: Uncertainty quoted as plus or minus a number
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type

@graph.definition: The type of uncertainty associated with the measurement is unknown.
@graph.schemeLabel: Geology Rock Properties - Statistical Uncertainty Type
